name: Persinger & Makarec 1987: 4 Hz field as a cue in card guessing
origin: Persinger & Makarec 1987 (Laurentian University), single-subject case study
summary: Zener-card guessing with a field cue: 40 trials of 30 s, with a 4 Hz sine field at both posterior temporal regions for the 30 s around each target card (the 15-s guessing interval and the 15 s the card is shown), on 8 of the 40 trials here. In Persinger & Makarec's single subject, guesses of the target stayed above chance (about 50% against 20%) only in sessions with the 4 Hz field, which they read as a learned cue.
notes: One subject guessed card symbols in 40 trials of 30 s. In each 15-s blank she pressed a button to predict the next symbol (mean latency about 10 s); then the slide showed for 15 s. The cue was 'a 4-Hz sine-wave field' on two pairs of solenoids at the caudal end of the helmet's matrix, over the posterior temporal lobes. It ran 30 s: the 15-s blank before the target (the star) and the 15 s the star was shown. The star came 4 to 8 times per session. On comparison days 1-Hz or 7-Hz sine fields were given in random positions (Persinger & Makarec 1987 p.1-2 [444-445]). This program plays a 4 Hz sine on both sides together for all 30 s of trials 4, 9, 11, 17, 22, 28, 31 and 37. The sine and the 30 s are as published. Its own choices: eight cues (the top of the paper's range), their positions, and the sites T7, TP7, T8 and TP8, inferred from 'caudal' and the matrix's 4-cm spacing. A helper keeps the 30-s clock from the program start and shows the star in the second half of each cued trial and another symbol on all other trials. Keep the app out of the subject's sight and mask coil sound. Before starting, run 0 to 4 extra uncued trials, a new random number each session, so that the cue positions cannot be learned. Field: 180 mG within 1 cm of the nearest solenoid and 5 mG at 4 cm inside the helmet (p.2 [445]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT this helmet's calculated field is about 44 mG at 10 mm and 1.8 mG at 40 mm, three to four times less than the paper's. One subject, no blinding reported, no replication. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Not for people with epilepsy.
setting: The subject sits facing the card display in a quiet room; the helper sits out of view with the app. Score hits on cued and uncued trials separately.
schedule: The original ran 17 sessions of 40 trials with one subject. Score each session, and include some Blind (possibly sham) sessions: with no field, cued trials should stay at chance.
source: Persinger & Makarec 1987, Possible learned detection of exogenous brain frequency electromagnetic fields: a case study, Percept Mot Skills 65:444-446 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3696915/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
